examples.ko: 가뭄이 길어지면 물 부족 현상이 심해져요.
examples.en: If the drought drags on, water shortages get worse.
In summer the days get longer.

examples.ko: 회의가 너무 길어져서 점심을 늦게 먹었어요.
examples.en: The meeting ran so long that I ate lunch late.
This story keeps getting longer.

examples.ko: 머리가 길어지니까 감을 때 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: Now that my hair is longer, washing it takes a long time.

examples.ko: 줄이 길어질 것 같으니까 일찍 가요.
examples.en: The line looks like it will get long, so let's go early.

explain: '길다'에 변화를 나타내는 '-아/어지다'가 붙은 말로, 길이뿐 아니라 시간, 말, 회의, 줄에도 써요. 반대말은 '짧아지다'예요. '늘어나다'는 수나 양이 많아질 때 쓰고, 시간이나 말이 오래 가는 것에는 '길어지다'가 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is '길다' plus the change ending '-아/어지다', and it works for length, time, talk, meetings and lines. The opposite is '짧아지다'. '늘어나다' is for numbers or amounts increasing, while '길어지다' fits things that last longer in time or talk.

examples.en: At night the temperature drops.
Interest rates have gone down lately, so loans got easier.

examples.ko: 시험이 너무 어려우면 평균 점수가 낮아질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the test is too hard, the average score can go down.
When you press the button, the desk slowly lowers.

examples.ko: 목소리가 낮아지면 화가 났다는 느낌이 들어요.
examples.en: When someone's voice gets low, it feels like they are angry.

examples.ko: 겨울이 되자 바닷물 온도가 많이 낮아졌어요.
examples.en: When winter came, the sea water temperature dropped a lot.

explain: '높아지다'의 반대말이고, 높이·온도·점수·수준처럼 위아래로 재는 것에 두루 써요. 소리는 '작아지다'와 달리 '낮아지다'라고 하면 음의 높낮이가 내려간다는 뜻이 돼요. 값이 내려갈 때는 '싸지다'나 '내려가다'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '높아지다' and works for anything measured up and down, such as height, temperature, scores and level. For voices, '낮아지다' means the pitch goes down, unlike '작아지다', which means quieter. For prices, people also say '싸지다' or '내려가다'.

examples.en: In the evening Mom cooks and I do the dishes.
I'm tired today, so I don't feel like cooking.
I got home from work and cooked right away.
On weekends Dad cooks for us.
While cooking the rice, I also boiled soup.

examples.ko: 밥할 시간이 없을 때는 햇반을 먹어요.
examples.en: When I have no time to cook, I eat instant rice.

explain: 쌀로 밥을 짓는 것이 기본이지만, 집에서 식사를 준비한다는 넓은 뜻으로도 자주 말해요. '밥을 짓다'는 조금 글 같은 느낌이고, 말할 때는 '밥하다'나 '밥을 하다'가 편해요. '요리하다'는 반찬이나 여러 음식을 만드는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: Its core meaning is cooking rice, but people often use it more broadly for preparing meals at home. '밥을 짓다' sounds a bit more written, so in speech '밥하다' or '밥을 하다' is natural. '요리하다' feels more like making side dishes or various foods.

en: become disgusted with; get sick of

examples.ko: 매일 같은 음식만 먹으니까 그 음식이 싫어져요.
examples.en: I eat the same food every day, so I'm getting sick of it.

examples.ko: 요즘 회사에 가는 게 점점 싫어지고 있어요.
examples.en: Lately I hate going to work more and more.

examples.ko: 친구가 거짓말을 한 뒤로 그 친구가 싫어졌어요.
examples.en: After my friend lied, I started to dislike that friend.

examples.ko: 너무 많이 먹으면 나중에 그 음식이 싫어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you eat too much, you may come to hate that food.
If studying suddenly becomes unbearable, take a short break.

examples.ko: 그 노래도 너무 자주 들으니까 싫어지더라고요.
examples.en: I heard that song so often that I got sick of it.

explain: '싫다'는 지금의 마음이고, '싫어지다'는 좋았거나 괜찮았던 것이 싫게 변했다는 뜻이에요. 반대말은 '좋아지다'예요. 같은 것을 너무 많이 해서 질릴 때는 '질리다'라고도 하는데, '싫어지다'는 음식·일뿐 아니라 사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: '싫다' is a present feeling, while '싫어지다' means something you liked or tolerated turned into something you dislike. The opposite is '좋아지다'. When you tire of something from overdoing it, '질리다' is also used, but '싫어지다' can be used for people as well as food or work.

examples.en: Autumn rain fell and the weather turned chilly.
Today the picnic was canceled because of the autumn rain.
I drank tea while watching the autumn rain outside the window.
The road is full of leaves wet from the autumn rain.
For autumn rain, it came down quite a lot.

examples.ko: 가을비 오는 날에는 따뜻한 국물이 생각나요.
examples.en: On autumn rainy days I crave something with warm broth.

explain: '봄비, 가을비, 겨울비'처럼 계절 이름에 '비'를 붙여 그 계절에 오는 비를 말해요. 발음은 쓴 대로 [가을비]예요. 가을비가 한 번 오면 날씨가 쌀쌀해졌다고 느끼는 경우가 많아서, 가을비 뒤에 겉옷을 챙기라는 말을 자주 해요.
explain_en: Like '봄비', '가을비' and '겨울비', you add '비' to a season name to mean rain of that season. It is pronounced as written, [가을비]. After autumn rain the air often feels noticeably cooler, so people may tell you to bring a jacket.

examples.ko: 처음에는 양을 채우고, 질은 그다음에 올려요.
examples.en: First you fill up the amount, and raise the quality after that.
Whose turn is next?
The next morning the rain stopped.

examples.ko: 이 길로 쭉 가서 그다음 사거리에서 오른쪽으로 가세요.
examples.en: Go straight along this road and turn right at the next intersection.
From then on, I'll take care of it myself.

examples.ko: 가장 중요한 건 건강이고, 그다음으로 가족이에요.
examples.en: The most important thing is health, and after that, family.

explain: '다음'은 그냥 뒤에 오는 것이고, '그다음'은 방금 말한 것이나 앞의 순서를 기준으로 바로 뒤를 가리켜요. 말할 때는 '그담에'로 줄여서 말하기도 해요. '그다음 날, 그다음 문제'처럼 뒤에 명사를 바로 붙여도 돼요.
explain_en: '다음' is simply what comes later, while '그다음' points to what comes right after the thing or step just mentioned. In speech it is often shortened to '그담에'. You can put a noun right after it, as in '그다음 날' or '그다음 문제'.

examples.en: There was leftover kimchi in the fridge, so I made kimchi fried rice.

examples.ko: 김치볶음밥에 계란 프라이를 올려 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: Kimchi fried rice is tasty with a fried egg on top.
For lunch I want to eat kimchi fried rice.

examples.ko: 김치볶음밥은 만들기 쉬워서 자주 해 먹어요.
examples.en: Kimchi fried rice is easy to make, so I cook it often.

examples.ko: 친구가 만든 김치볶음밥 맛이 정말 좋았어요.
examples.en: The kimchi fried rice my friend made tasted really good.

examples.ko: 여기요, 김치볶음밥 하나랑 라면 하나 주세요.
examples.en: Excuse me, one kimchi fried rice and one ramyeon, please.

explain: 김치를 넣고 볶은 밥이에요. 집에서는 '만들다'나 '해 먹다'를 쓰고, 식당에서는 '시키다'나 '주문하다'를 써요. 새우볶음밥, 야채볶음밥처럼 앞에 재료를 붙여 다른 볶음밥도 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is fried rice stir-fried with kimchi. At home people say '만들다' or '해 먹다', and at a restaurant '시키다' or '주문하다'. You can put other ingredients in front, as in 새우볶음밥 or 야채볶음밥, to name other fried rice dishes.

examples.en: On rainy days I think of kimchi pancakes.

examples.ko: 김치전을 부칠 때는 기름을 넉넉히 둘러요.
examples.en: When you pan-fry kimchi pancakes, use plenty of oil.
If you add onion to the kimchi pancake, it gets sweeter.
We dip kimchi pancakes in soy sauce.

examples.ko: 우리 김치전 한 장 더 시킬까요?
examples.en: Shall we order one more kimchi pancake?
I had a kimchi pancake together with bean sprout soup.

explain: 김치를 넣어 얇게 부친 음식이에요. 만들 때는 '굽다'보다 '부치다'를 써서 '전을 부치다'라고 해요. '김치부침개'도 같은 음식을 가리키는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a thin pancake pan-fried with kimchi. When making it, you say '전을 부치다' rather than '굽다'. '김치부침개' is another name for the same dish.

examples.en: One plus two is three.
Five plus five is ten.

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 더하기와 빼기를 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: My child is learning addition and subtraction.
Addition is easy, but division is hard.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 더하기 문제라서 금방 풀었어요.
examples.en: This was an addition problem, so I solved it quickly.
I drew a big plus sign on the board.

explain: '3 + 4'는 '삼 더하기 사'처럼 읽고, 숫자는 한자어(일, 이, 삼)로 말해요. 짝말은 '빼기, 곱하기, 나누기'예요. 계산기나 기호를 말할 때는 '플러스'도 쓰지만, 수학 시간에는 '더하기'가 기본이에요.
explain_en: You read '3 + 4' as '삼 더하기 사', using Sino-Korean numbers (일, 이, 삼). Its partners are 빼기, 곱하기 and 나누기. '플러스' is also used for the sign or on a calculator, but in math class '더하기' is the basic word.

examples.ko: 재워 둔 돼지갈비를 오늘 저녁에 구워 먹어요.
examples.en: We'll grill the marinated pork ribs tonight.
Excuse me, two servings of pork ribs, please.
This place's pork ribs have a sweet marinade.

examples.ko: 돼지갈비에 밥도 한 공기 같이 주세요.
examples.en: With the pork ribs, please also give me a bowl of rice.
Pork ribs are cheaper than beef ribs.
I had pork ribs for lunch, so I'm full.

explain: 돼지고기의 갈비 부분을 양념해 구워 먹는 음식을 말해요. '소갈비'와 달리 돼지고기라서 값이 보통 더 부담 없어요. 불판에 구워 상추에 싸 먹는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It refers to marinated pork ribs, usually grilled. Unlike '소갈비' (beef ribs), it is pork, so it is usually the cheaper choice. People often grill it at the table and wrap it in lettuce.

examples.en: If the pot gets too hot, turn down the heat.
Wait until the frying pan gets hot.
When I turned on the heater, the room got hot quickly.
The soup had cooled, so I reheated it and it got hot.
When it's midday, the sand gets too hot.

examples.ko: 햇볕에 있었더니 팔이 뜨거워지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: After being in the sun, my arms feel like they are heating up.

explain: '뜨겁다'는 손이나 몸에 닿는 열이 셀 때 써서, 날씨가 더울 때 쓰는 '더워지다'와 달라요. '따뜻해지다'는 기분 좋게 따뜻한 정도이고, 반대말은 '차가워지다'나 '식다'예요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '뜨거워요, 뜨거워져요'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: I remembered my mistake and my face burned with embarrassment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 열이 나는 게 아니라 창피하거나 부끄러울 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not mean a real fever; it is used when you feel embarrassed or ashamed.

explain_en: '뜨겁다' is about heat you feel by touch, unlike '더워지다', which is for hot weather. '따뜻해지다' is a pleasant warmth, and the opposites are '차가워지다' or '식다'. It is a ㅂ-irregular word, so it becomes '뜨거워요' and '뜨거워져요'.

examples.ko: 추운 날에는 따뜻한 만둣국이 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: On cold days I want to eat warm dumpling soup.

examples.ko: 설날 아침에 떡국 대신 만둣국을 먹기도 해요.
examples.en: On New Year's morning some people eat dumpling soup instead of rice cake soup.
If you stir an egg into the dumpling soup, it gets softer.
One bowl of dumpling soup here, please.

examples.ko: 만둣국은 만두가 커서 한 그릇이면 배불러요.
examples.en: The dumplings in this soup are big, so one bowl fills you up.
I took care of dinner simply with dumpling soup.

explain: 만두를 넣고 끓인 국이에요. 글자는 'ㅅ'이 있지만 '만둗꾹'처럼 발음해서 'ㄱ'이 된소리로 나요. 떡을 넣으면 '떡국', 둘 다 넣으면 '떡만둣국'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a soup boiled with dumplings. The spelling has 'ㅅ' but you pronounce it '만둗꾹', with 'ㄱ' turning tense. With rice cakes it is '떡국', and with both it is '떡만둣국'.

examples.ko: 여름에는 해수욕장마다 파라솔과 튜브를 빌려주는 가게가 생겨요.
examples.en: In summer, shops that rent out parasols and tubes appear at every beach.

examples.ko: 친구가 비 오는 날 우산을 빌려줬어요.
examples.en: My friend lent me an umbrella on a rainy day.
It's heavy, so could you lend me a hand?
It's hard to lend money even to a close friend.

examples.ko: 제 노트를 빌려줄 테니까 복사해서 쓰세요.
examples.en: I'll lend you my notes, so copy them and use them.

examples.ko: 도서관에서는 책을 이 주 동안 빌려줘요.
examples.en: The library lends books for two weeks.

explain: '빌리다'는 받는 쪽, '빌려주다'는 주는 쪽이에요. 윗사람에게 줄 때는 '빌려 드리다'라고 해요. 돈이나 물건을 빌려주고 받는 일은 '빌리다-빌려주다'를 짝으로 기억하면 쉬워요.

phrases.en: My friends lent a hand on moving day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 손을 주는 게 아니라 일을 도와준다는 뜻이에요. 부탁할 때는 '손 좀 빌려주세요'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: No hand is actually lent; it means helping with a task. When asking, you say '손 좀 빌려주세요'.

explain_en: '빌리다' is the borrowing side and '빌려주다' is the lending side. When the receiver is older or senior, say '빌려 드리다'. It helps to remember the pair '빌리다-빌려주다'.

en: studying for a test; exam study

examples.ko: 시험공부를 할 때 단원마다 핵심어를 따로 적어 두면 편해요.
examples.en: When studying for a test, it's handy to note key words for each unit.

examples.ko: 시험공부는 도서관에서 하는 게 집중이 잘돼요.
examples.en: Studying for exams at the library helps me concentrate.
I'm not getting enough sleep because of exam study.
When you study for a test, keep your phone far away.
I turned off my phone to focus on studying for the test.

examples.ko: 시험공부가 끝나면 영화를 보러 갈 거예요.
examples.en: When I'm done studying for the exam, I'll go see a movie.

explain: 시험을 위해 하는 공부를 말해요. 시험 전날 한꺼번에 몰아서 하는 것은 '벼락치기'라고 하는데, 영어의 cramming에 더 가까운 말이에요. '시험공부를 하다'가 가장 자연스럽고, 가까운 말로 '시험 준비'가 있어요.
explain_en: It means study done for a test. Doing it all at once the night before is called '벼락치기', which is closer to English 'cramming'. '시험공부를 하다' is the most natural phrase, and a related expression is '시험 준비'.

examples.en: Yesterday evening I watched a movie with a friend.
My head has been hurting since last evening.
Did you watch the nine o'clock news last evening?
Last evening it rained a lot.
I'm really sorry about what happened last evening.
Up until last evening the weather was fine.

explain: '어젯밤'은 잠자기 전 늦은 시간의 느낌이 강하고, '어제저녁'은 저녁 식사 무렵처럼 조금 이른 시간을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 뒤에 '에'를 붙이거나 생략해도 돼요. '어제 저녁'처럼 띄어 쓴 형태로도 많이 봐요.
explain_en: '어젯밤' feels like late hours close to bedtime, while '어제저녁' suits an earlier time, around dinner. You can add '에' after it or leave it out. You will also often see it written with a space, as '어제 저녁'.

examples.en: We eat dinner together as a family.
What shall we eat for dinner today?
Mom has set out dinner and is waiting.
I'll finish my homework before dinner.

examples.ko: 저녁밥이 다 식기 전에 어서 오세요.
examples.en: Come quickly before dinner gets cold.
I was busy and worked without even eating dinner.

explain: '저녁'만 말해도 저녁 식사를 뜻할 때가 많고, '저녁밥'은 밥이라는 음식을 조금 더 느끼게 하는 편한 말이에요. 격식 있는 자리에서는 '저녁 식사'가 어울려요. '아침밥, 점심밥, 저녁밥'을 세트로 기억하면 좋아요.
explain_en: Just saying '저녁' can already mean the evening meal, while '저녁밥' is a casual word that puts more focus on the meal itself. In formal settings, '저녁 식사' fits better. It helps to learn '아침밥, 점심밥, 저녁밥' as a set.

examples.en: I eat lunch at a restaurant near my office.
What did you eat for lunch today?

examples.ko: 동생이 점심밥을 먹고 바로 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling ate lunch and went straight to school.

examples.ko: 점심밥 먹을 시간도 없을 만큼 바빴어요.
examples.en: I was so busy I didn't even have time for lunch.
I brought gimbap for lunch.

examples.ko: 학교 점심밥이 맛있어서 한 그릇 더 먹었어요.
examples.en: The school lunch was tasty, so I had another bowl.

explain: 보통은 그냥 '점심'이라고 하고, '점심밥'은 밥 먹는 것을 조금 더 구체적으로 말하는 편한 표현이에요. 격식 있게는 '점심 식사'라고 해요. 싸 가지고 가는 점심은 '도시락'이라고 해요.
explain_en: People usually just say '점심', and '점심밥' is a casual way to talk about the meal more concretely. The formal version is '점심 식사'. A packed lunch you carry along is called '도시락'.

examples.ko: 지갑을 안 가져와서 주인아저씨께 외상을 부탁했어요.
examples.en: I didn't bring my wallet, so I asked the owner to let me pay later.
The owner gave us a free drink.
The owner of this shop is always kind.

examples.ko: 주인아저씨, 여기 물 좀 더 주세요.
examples.en: Sir, could we get some more water here?
I decided the moving date with the landlord.
I asked the stationery shop owner for directions.

explain: 동네 가게나 식당의 남자 주인을 친근하게 부르거나 말하는 표현이에요. 부를 때는 '사장님'이 더 정중하고 많이 써요. 여자 주인은 '주인아주머니'라고 하고, 집의 주인은 '집주인'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a friendly way to call or talk about a male owner of a neighborhood shop or restaurant. When addressing someone, '사장님' is more polite and very common. A female owner is '주인아주머니', and the owner of a house can also be called '집주인'.

examples.en: I fell asleep watching TV in the living room.

examples.ko: 티브이 소리가 너무 커서 이야기를 못 했어요.
examples.en: The TV was so loud that we couldn't talk.
Our TV suddenly turned off.
I heard today's weather news on TV.

examples.ko: 티브이는 밥 먹을 때 끄는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to turn the TV off when eating.

examples.ko: 새 티브이로 바꿨더니 화면이 훨씬 선명해요.
examples.en: I switched to a new TV and the picture is much clearer.

explain: '텔레비전'을 줄여 한글로 쓴 말로, 영어 TV를 읽은 소리예요. 말할 때는 '티비'라고도 많이 하는데, 글에서는 '티브이'나 'TV'로 써요. '티브이를 보다/켜다/끄다'처럼 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is the Hangul spelling of the sound of English 'TV', short for '텔레비전'. In speech people often say '티비', but in writing it is '티브이' or 'TV'. It pairs with verbs as in '티브이를 보다/켜다/끄다'.

examples.ko: 신입생은 학교생활을 알기 위해서 선배에게 질문해요.
examples.en: New students ask seniors questions to learn about school life.

examples.ko: 학부모 상담 때 담임에게 아이의 학교생활을 자세히 물어봤어요.
examples.en: At the parent meeting I asked the homeroom teacher in detail about my child's school life.
School life is fun, but there is a lot of homework.
At my new school, school life still feels unfamiliar.
Once I made friends, school life became enjoyable.

examples.ko: 학교생활 중에서 소풍이 제일 기억에 남아요.
examples.en: Of all my school life, the field trip is what I remember most.

explain: 학교에 다니면서 겪는 수업, 친구, 행사 같은 전체 생활을 말해요. '학교생활을 하다'보다 '학교생활이 재미있다/힘들다', '학교생활에 적응하다'처럼 자주 말해요. 대학교에서는 '대학 생활'이라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It covers everything about attending school: classes, friends and events. People more often say '학교생활이 재미있다/힘들다' or '학교생활에 적응하다' than '학교생활을 하다'. For university, '대학 생활' is the common phrase.
